---
title: "D3 Model dependencies"
---

## The score spine

One model feeds every other component. The Business Credit Score is computed once, by
its own scoring function (`predict_score_pd`), and every consumer calls that function
rather than re-implementing it.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  G["Data generator"] --> S["D4 Score<br/>score · PD · band"]
  S --> A["D5 Adjudication"]
  S --> P["D6 Pricing"]
  S --> E["D7 Early Warning"]
  S --> L["D8 Line Increase"]
  M["Market assumptions<br/>shared.config.MARKET"] --> P
  M --> L
  A --> UI["Portal (app/)"]
  P --> UI
  E --> UI
  L --> UI
```

Every module also reads the generator's data directly, for its own features and
population; the diagram shows only what flows between components.

| Consumer | What it takes from the score | Population |
|---|---|---|
| D5 Loan Adjudication | `business_score` and `pd_score` as two of its inputs; the band for the policy layer | applicants |
| D6 Pricing | the PD, as the expected-loss term of the rate | booked |
| D7 Early Warning | `business_score` and `pd_score` as inputs, beside behavioural features | booked |
| D8 Line Increase | `pd_score` as an input and as the risk-appetite cut | booked |

Pricing also depends on the market assumptions in `shared.config.MARKET`, and line
increase uses the same hurdle for its incremental-ROE test. Neither is a model; both are
policy values under change control (D9).

The portal (`app/`) orchestrates the modules and never re-implements them: every number
it shows comes from the module's own function. A disagreement between the portal and a
module is treated as a defect. `verify.py` smoke-tests the portal on every run, and
checks that an adjudication requested through the loan workbench equals the batch
decision for the same applicant.

## What a scorecard change forces

Because the score is an input everywhere, a change to it — rebinning, a new feature, a
refit on new data — is a change to every consumer, even if no consumer's code moves.

| Consumer | What must be redone | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D5 Loan Adjudication | retrain; recalibrate the PD zones; re-assert its gate | the score is one of its inputs, and the policy cutoffs are set from the model's PD distribution at training time |
| D6 Pricing | re-run over the booked book; re-read the mispricing summary | every recommended rate moves with the PD |
| D7 Early Warning | retrain; recalibrate the tier cutoffs; re-assert its gate | the score is an input and the tiers are set from the fitted probabilities |
| D8 Line Increase | retrain; recalibrate the offer cutoff; re-assert its gate | the score is an input and sets who is eligible |
| The portal and this documentation | `python verify.py` | it recomputes every gate and every fact on these pages |

A change is complete only when `python verify.py` passes on the result. Its checks run in
dependency order — data, score, adjudication, early warning, line increase, documentation,
portal — and each failure is reported by name, so a scorecard change that breaks a
consumer shows up at that consumer.
